## Setup

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

evals <- read.csv(
  "https://www.openintro.org/data/csv/evals.csv"
)
```

# Exercises

## Exercise 1: Start with the simple relationship

```{r}
ggplot(
  evals,
  aes(x = bty_avg, y = score)
) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0,
    height = 0.05,
    alpha = 0.40
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Average attractiveness rating",
    y = "Average evaluation score",
    title = "Professor evaluations and attractiveness ratings"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Describe the direction and strength of the relationship.

> 

Why is `geom_jitter()` useful here?

> 

Does the graph establish causation? Explain.

> 

## Exercise 2: Simple regression

```{r}
m1 <- lm(
  score ~ bty_avg,
  data = evals
)

summary(m1)
```

Write the fitted regression equation.

> 

Interpret the coefficient on `bty_avg`.

> 

What might this simple model be leaving out?

> 

## Exercise 3: Add gender

```{r}
m2 <- lm(
  score ~ bty_avg + gender,
  data = evals
)

summary(m2)
```

What happened to the coefficient on `bty_avg` after adding gender?

> 

Interpret the `bty_avg` coefficient using **holding gender constant**.

> 

Why can coefficients change when another predictor is added?

>

## Exercise 5: Predicted values

```{r}
professors <- data.frame(
  bty_avg = c(5, 5),
  gender = c("female", "male")
)

professors |>
  mutate(
    predicted_score = predict(
      m2,
      newdata = professors
    )
  )
```

What is being held constant?

> 

What differs between the two cases?

> 

Report and interpret the predicted scores.

> 

How does the difference relate to the `gendermale` coefficient?

>

## Exercise 7: Add age

```{r}
m4 <- lm(
  score ~ bty_avg + gender + age,
  data = evals
)

summary(m4)
```

Compare the attractiveness coefficient:

```{r}
data.frame(
  model = c(
    "Beauty only",
    "Beauty + gender",
    "Beauty + gender + age"
  ),
  bty_coefficient = c(
    coef(m1)["bty_avg"],
    coef(m2)["bty_avg"],
    coef(m4)["bty_avg"]
  )
)
```

How does the `bty_avg` coefficient change?

> 

Interpret `bty_avg` in `m4`.

> 

Interpret the coefficient on `age`.

> 

Why do you need to know what else is in the model before interpreting a coefficient?

>

```{r}
  mutate(

```

## Exercise 9: Predict across a range

Fit the additive model:

```{r}
m5 <- lm(
  score ~ bty_avg + gender,
  data = evals
)

summary(m5)
```

First predict across attractiveness ratings for male professors only:

```{r}
prediction_grid_male <- expand.grid(
  bty_avg = seq(1, 8),
  gender = "male"
)

preds_male <- predict(
  m5,
  newdata = prediction_grid_male,
  interval = "confidence"
)

graph_preds_male <- bind_cols(
  prediction_grid_male,
  as.data.frame(preds_male)
)
```

Graph the predictions:

```{r}
ggplot(
  graph_preds_male,
  aes(
    x = bty_avg,
    y = fit
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(
    x = "Average attractiveness rating",
    y = "Predicted evaluation score",
    title = "Predicted course evaluations",
    subtitle = "Predicted scores for male professors"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

What does the line show?

> 

How is its slope related to the `bty_avg` coefficient?

> 

## Exercise 10: Compare both gender groups

```{r}
prediction_grid_all <- expand.grid(
  bty_avg = seq(1, 8),
  gender = c("female", "male")
)

preds_all <- predict(
  m5,
  newdata = prediction_grid_all,
  interval = "confidence"
)

graph_preds_all <- bind_cols(
  prediction_grid_all,
  as.data.frame(preds_all)
)
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  graph_preds_all,
  aes(
    x = bty_avg,
    y = fit,
    color = gender
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(
    x = "Average attractiveness rating",
    y = "Predicted evaluation score",
    color = "Gender",
    title = "Predicted course evaluations",
    subtitle = "Across attractiveness ratings and gender"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Are the lines parallel?

> 

What does the vertical distance between them represent?

> 

Why does this model assume the same beauty slope for both groups?

> 

## Exercise 11: Interaction

Now allow the relationship between attractiveness and evaluation score to differ by gender.

```{r}
m5_int <- lm(
  score ~ bty_avg * gender,
  data = evals
)

summary(m5_int)
```

```{r}
prediction_grid_int <- expand.grid(
  bty_avg = seq(1, 8),
  gender = c("female", "male")
)

preds_int <- predict(
  m5_int,
  newdata = prediction_grid_int,
  interval = "confidence"
)

graph_preds_int <- bind_cols(
  prediction_grid_int,
  as.data.frame(preds_int)
)
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  graph_preds_int,
  aes(
    x = bty_avg,
    y = fit,
    color = gender
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(
    x = "Average attractiveness rating",
    y = "Predicted evaluation score",
    color = "Gender",
    title = "Predicted course evaluations",
    subtitle = "Allowing the attractiveness slope to differ by gender"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

How does this graph differ from the additive-model graph?

> 

What does it mean if the slopes differ?

> 

What new question does the interaction model allow us to ask?

>
